name: Placentalia
blurb: Mammals whose young develop to an advanced stage inside the mother, nourished through a placenta. Where the root of their tree lies is one of the classic open questions in mammal evolution.

relationship.note: The three major lineages are well supported. Which of them split off first is not settled: the three possible answers each have support from different datasets and analyses.

competing.name: Atlantogenata
competing.summary: Afrotheria and Xenarthra are each other's closest relatives, as two southern-continent radiations.

competing.name: Exafroplacentalia
competing.summary: Afrotheria split off first; Xenarthra is closer to Boreoeutheria.

competing.name: Epitheria
competing.summary: Xenarthra split off first; Afrotheria is closer to Boreoeutheria.

softMax.basis: Divergence of Eutheria from other mammals, marked by Juramaia (Tiaojishan Formation, Oxfordian): base of the Oxfordian, 163.5 ± 1.1 Ma
softMax.checked: Benton et al. 2015, full text (palaeo-electronica.org/content/pdfs/424.pdf), node 60 (Crown Placentalia)

clock.method: Bayesian relaxed molecular clock (MCMCTree), posterior mean and 95% HPD

fossilMin.dating: Early Puercan, earliest Danian; treated as early Paleocene, top 61.7 ± 0.1 Ma gives 61.6 Ma
fossilMin.checked: Benton et al. 2015, full text (palaeo-electronica.org/content/pdfs/424.pdf), node 60 (Crown Placentalia)
